I'm working through the coordinates of chain C's residues to identify which atoms are positioned to make contact with chain A.

Still listing atomic coordinates...

Still writing coordinates...

Now I need to check chain A against chain C's spatial range, scanning for atoms that fall within proximity based on their y-coordinates.

I'm grouping chain C residues by their approximate x/y/z location to make it easier to spot which chain A residues might be close enough to contact them: ALA1/ARG2 sit around x -14 to -18, THR3 near x -14, LYS4 around x -9 to -12, GLN5 near x -9 to -11.

Then I extend this mapping through THR6, ALA7, ARG8, M3L9, and SER10, tracking their coordinate ranges, and start scanning chain A's atom list to find ones with y below -5 that could be near these chain C residues.

Now checking chain C M3L9 coordinates against TYR203's OH position, computing the distance between OH and the CE atom of M3L to see if they're close enough to interact.

I confirm that distance is under 4 Å, so residue 203 tyrosine does contact this region. Now I'm systematically scanning chain A residues within the relevant coordinate bounds, checking ASN199's atom positions but finding its x-coordinate too large to be near chain C's contact zone.

Continuing through CYS200 and LYS202, both are too far based on their coordinates. For TYR203, I'm now checking individual side-chain atoms against M3L residue atoms, calculating distances between CD1/CE1 carbons and the CE/CD carbons on the lysine methyl group to see which pairs fall within the 4 Å contact threshold.

CZ and CE2 on TYR203 both come out under 4 Å from M3L's CE/CM2 atoms, confirming this residue makes contact. Now I'm moving to TYR204, listing out its backbone and side-chain coordinates (N, CA, CB, CG, CD1/CD2, CE1/CE2, CZ, OH) to begin the same distance comparison.

Checking TYR204 against M3L's NZ, CM3, and CM2, none of the distances fall under 4 Å — the closest, N to CM2, comes to 4.73 Å, and the others follow a similar pattern, so this residue doesn't qualify as a contact. Moving on to MET205, I'm pulling its N, CA, and CB coordinates to start the same check.

For SER206, though, I find two hits: OG comes within 3.70 Å of M3L's CM2 and 3.90 Å of CM1, so I'm marking A:S206 as a genuine contact. I'll continue this same distance-checking process for ASP207 next.

Checking ASP208's remaining atoms against nearby CM1, computing distances to see if it falls within the 4Å contact cutoff.

After running through the math, CM3 to the O atom of ASP208 comes out to about 3.90Å, which is within range - so that's a contact.

Now I'm moving to residue 209 ILE, checking its atom coordinates against nearby chain C atoms to see what else might be close enough to count.

CM3 to ILE209 CG1 gives a distance of about 3.77, under the 4Å cutoff, so that's another contact: A:I209. I'm now checking the other ILE209 atoms (CB, CA) against CM3 to see if they also fall within range, though CB comes out slightly over 4Å.

Moving to SER210, I'm pulling coordinates for N, CA, C, O, CB, OG and comparing against the nearby chain residues, but the z-coordinates seem too far off from ARG8's region to suggest a contact.

Checking M3L's CG and CD atoms against OG doesn't reveal any close distances either, so I'm ruling out residue 210 as a contact point and moving on to residue 211, ARG, to check its coordinates against other regions of chain A.

Continuing through residues 212-216, I'm scanning ASP, SER, GLY, and MET coordinates and none of their z-values come close to chain C's minimum z of -8.6, so these residues stay out of contact range too.

Then checking MET216's carbon and oxygen positions against chain C's ARG2 side chain — the CG-to-NH1 distance comes out around 4.4Å, still too far. But testing LYS4's NZ against MET216's carbonyl oxygen, I get a distance close to 3.67Å, which is under the 4Å cutoff — this looks like a real contact worth flagging.

Moving on to ASP217's atoms, I'm checking LYS4's NZ against its backbone oxygen and get roughly 2.59Å apart — clearly another valid contact — while the distance to the alpha carbon comes out closer to 3Å.

Continuing to GLU218, I calculate NZ against its backbone nitrogen and get about 4.52Å, which falls just outside the cutoff, so no contact there. I start scanning GLN5 and THR6 coordinates for additional nearby atoms.

Checking O against THR6's OG1, the distance comes to 2.69Å, well under the threshold—confirming a contact between A:E218 and THR6. I move on to GLN219's backbone atoms next.

I'm checking distances between GLN219 and THR6 atoms, and none of these pairings seem close enough to form a contact—so GLN219 likely isn't involved here. I'll move on to check GLN5's coordinates next.

Now checking CYS220's atom positions against nearby chain residues like ARG8, but nothing in this y-coordinate range appears close enough for a contact either.

Checking ALA224's coordinates against chain C candidates again finds no match, so I continue to residue 225 GLU, computing its backbone atom positions.

That distance also confirms the contact at 3.90Å, and the CD-to-ARG8 CG distance of 3.97Å is another confirmed contact under the 4Å cutoff. Now I'm checking the coordinates for GLY226's backbone atoms.

Checking ARG8's CG, CZ, and NH2 atoms against GLY226's N, C, and O positions, most distances come out too far except NE to O, which gives 3.41Å — that's a confirmed contact between chain A and GLY226. Now I'm verifying by re-checking the CA to ARG8 CG distance.

Moving to residue 227, I'm running the same distance calculations between ARG8's guanidinium atoms and GLY227's backbone atoms, finding CZ to CA at 3.70Å confirms a contact, while NH2 to CA sits right at the borderline around 4.06Å.

Continuing to residue 228 (ASN), I'm gathering its backbone and side chain coordinates, then checking distances against nearby atoms from chain C's GLN5, particularly its CG, CD, OE1, and NE2 positions to see if this forms another contact pair.

Checking ASN228's CA against OE1 gives a distance under 4 angstroms, confirming another A-chain to N228 contact.

Now I'm pulling coordinates for the next residue, LEU229, gathering its backbone atoms and side chain positions including the branched CD1/CD2 carbons.

I'm scanning chain C candidates near LEU229 for possible contacts—checking LYS4, THR3, and GLN5 distances, all coming up too far. Then I try LEU229's CD1 against THR6's CG2, and the distance calculation comes out right at the 4.0 boundary, so I want to double-check that borderline case more carefully.

Recomputing precisely, LEU229 CD1 to THR6 CG2 gives 3.998, just barely qualifying as a contact. Checking other LEU229 atoms against THR6, the CG-to-OG1 distance is too far at 4.11, but CD1-to-OG1 comes out to 3.66, clearly confirming LEU229 does contact this residue.

Moving to residue 230, ILE, I lay out its backbone and side chain coordinates and start checking distances to chain C residues near that region, but THR3's CG2 to ILE230's CG1 comes out to 4.17, too far.

For 231 CYS, I map out its coordinates including SG, then test proximity to chain C's ARG2 side chain atoms and LYS4's CD — the SG to LYS4 CD distance comes out to 3.57, under the 4 cutoff, so I'm confirming A:C231 as a contact.

Moving to 232 CYS, I lay out its backbone and CB/SG positions, then check against chain C's y-coordinate range and find nothing close enough — ruling this residue out. I'm starting to look at 233 ASP's coordinates next.

Continuing to scan chain A residues 234-238 for atoms falling into the x/y/z window around chain C's ALA1/ARG2, I check 213 SER and 214 ASP but their z-coordinates put them too far from chain C's range.

Checking 241 LYS coordinates against chain C's max z values - the distances are too far in x, so no match. Moving to check 250 ARG's CG coordinates next.

Since none of these residues (250-262) line up with ALA1 or ARG2 of chain C, I need to look elsewhere in chain A. ALA1 sits around (-17,-2,-1.5) and ARG2 around (-16,-6,-4), so I'm scanning chain A residues 254-258 for atoms near that x -15 to -20, y -2 to -8, z -2 to -8 range.

I check ILE256 and find its backbone oxygen sits about 3.56 angstroms from ALA1's CB — close enough to count as a contact between chain A's ILE256 and chain C's ALA1.

Now checking MET257's coordinates against ALA1's nitrogen, but the z-distance from the carbon looks too large for a contact there.

But THR3's CG2 comes within range of MET257's SD atom, distance about 3.64 Å — that's a valid contact. The CE atom of MET257 also falls within contact distance of THR3's CG2, roughly 3.63 Å.

Checking ARG2's CA against ALA1's CB shows too large a gap. I look at ASP258's atoms and find they're all too far from chain C's nearest points, well over 5 Å away, so no contact there. Now I'm shifting to check which chain A residues might be close to ARG2's side chain.

I'm scanning CYS231's sulfur and beta-carbon positions against ARG2's CG and CB atoms, but the distances come out around 4.2-4.3 Å, still too far to count. ASP214 doesn't look promising either based on its coordinates, so I'm turning to LEU253 next to see if its side chain atoms fall within range.

Now I'm checking the pocket near LYS4 and GLN5, examining chain A residues 215-241 in that x/y/z window, comparing GLY215's nitrogen position and moving through ILE230 and into ALA238's backbone atoms to see if any fall close enough to matter.

GLY227 O is within 4Å of THR6 OG1, confirming that contact. Now checking GLU225's OE1 against nearby ARG8 and M3L residues to see if any distances fall under the cutoff.

Then I catch something: ALA224's O is only 3.33Å from M3L's CM3, which is a valid contact I need to include. This makes me realize I should go back and systematically recheck the whole region near M3L more carefully, since I may have missed similar close contacts.

Now I'm scanning through chain A residues sequentially, checking y-coordinates and other distances against the M3L/ARG8 region to catch any contacts I might have overlooked around residues 199 through 203 and beyond.

Continuing residue by residue: SER206's OG is close enough to include, though its other atoms aren't near CM2; ASP207 also gets included at y -8.3 to -12.6, and I'm now verifying its backbone nitrogen distance against CM1.

I'm moving on to check ASP208 (included via O-CM3), ILE209 (included), and now SER210, where I'm computing whether its OG and CB atoms fall within range of the M3L CD atom.

Checking further residues: ARG211 through 215 appear too deep in z to be close, but MET216, ASP217, and GLU218 are included. Now I'm examining GLN219's side chain atoms against nearby chain C atoms to see if any fall within the M3L contact distance.

Recomputing the M3L CD to GLN219 NE2 distance gives about 3.96 Å, just under the 4 Å cutoff, so it counts as a contact. Checking M3L CG to the same NE2 atom gives an even tighter 3.90 Å, confirming GLN219 belongs on the contact list.

Now I'm moving to CYS220, checking whether any of its atoms near y -4 to -7.2 fall close enough to chain C, possibly ARG2 given its position.

Continuing residue by residue: CYS220 doesn't seem to make contact with THR6, and ARG221, TRP222 are excluded since their y-coordinates are too positive. For CYS223 I'm checking SG and O against nearby atoms in chain C like CM3 and M3L NZ, finding the distances too large to count. ALA224 does qualify though — its CB atom sits about 3.97 Å from CM3, just inside the cutoff. I'm marking GLU225, GLY226, GLY227, ASN228, LEU229, and CYS231 as included, while ILE230 and CYS232 are excluded, and now working through residues 233 onward checking their y-coordinates against the contact threshold.

For residues 234-241 I'm systematically checking each one's coordinates against nearby chain C atoms — PHE234, CYS235, HIS236, ASN237, ALA238, and PHE239 all fail the y or z distance criteria against chain C residues like THR6 and ARG8. CYS240 and LYS241 also come up short: LYS241's NZ atom gets close to THR3's CG2 and OG1 in chain C but the z-distance still pushes it just outside 4 Å, so I'm ruling it out and moving on to check LYS242's CG coordinates next.

Now checking LYS242's remaining atoms — CD and CE are too far from chain C, but NZ at (-1.804,-10.729,6.584) comes within 3.91 Å of ARG8's NH1 atom in chain C, confirming a genuine contact for K242. I've verified this distance twice and also ruled out CE as a contact since it's just over 4 Å, so K242 is confirmed. Moving on, CYS243, ILE244 fail the distance checks, and I'm starting to examine LEU245's CB coordinates next.

I'm scanning chain A residues 255-257 for atoms falling within that x/y/z range near ALA1 of chain C, checking ILE256, MET257, and THR255 coordinates but none seem to match the target y-value.

Checking ASP233 and PHE234, their z-values are also too far off, roughly 6 units away from ALA1's position. It looks like only ILE256's O atom is close enough, meaning ALA1 might be mostly solvent exposed, so I'll move on to check ARG2's CB atom against nearby chain A atoms.

Nothing in that region matches either - MET257, ASP214, SER213 are all too far in z. I'm now cross-checking ASP233's coordinates against ARG2 more carefully to see if there's a closer contact I'm missing.

Confirmed the 3.79 distance, so ASP233 OD1 contacts ALA1 CA. Checking OD2 against the same residue's CA and CB, both come out beyond 4 (4.07 and 4.50), so those don't count as contacts.

I need to be more systematic here rather than checking one-off distances. My plan is to sweep through chain A by spatial region, matching each cluster of chain C residues to nearby chain A neighborhoods — starting with the region covering ALA1 and ARG2.

I'm checking chain A atoms with x < -13, looking through residues 213 and 214 (SER213, ASP214) to see which ones fall in range, but ASP214's side chain sits too far in z from ARG2 to be a real contact.

Now I'm continuing with ASP233, checking its CA, CB, CG, and carboxylate oxygens for proximity to ALA1's CA — the distances turn out too large in dy and dz to count. Moving to PHE234, its backbone nitrogen falls just within the x<-13 cutoff.

Checking PHE234's full ring atoms (CA, CB, CG through CZ) against ALA1's N and CD2 coordinates — the y-values are too positive and distances too far to be relevant. I rule out ARG250/251 since their z-coordinates run too high, and I move on to inspect SER254's CA position next.

Working through THR255, then ILE256 — I find a real contact between ILE256's C/O atoms and something in ALA1's chain. I continue checking MET257's backbone and sidechain atoms (CA, C, O, CB, CG, SD, CE) against ALA1's CB position to see if that's another close contact.

Checking MET257's SD and CE distances to THR3 — most are just over 5 Å, so no contact there either. I then move to ASP258's CA, CB, and CG positions, which are far enough from ALA1's coordinates to rule out.

I continue scanning further residues — GLU259, GLN262, TRP263 — comparing their backbone and side chain atoms against ALA1's N atom, but the distances keep coming out too large (mostly 5+ Å) to count as contacts.

So the candidate contacts for this region settle on I256, M257, and D233 near ALA1's CA. I move on to check CYS231/232 against ARG2's carbon atoms.

Checking distances from ARG2's CB, CG, CD, and O atoms to nearby chain A residues like CYS231's CB and SG, and MET257's SD, but none of these come close enough to count as real contacts.

Checking a few more distances - ARG2 O to ILE230 turns out too far, but ARG2 O to CYS231 CA comes in at 3.61, so that's another valid contact. Now I'm checking ARG2 N against nearby chain A residues to find its closest partner.

Turning to THR3, I'm calculating distances from its various atoms (CA, CB, OG1, CG2, N, C, O) against chain A residues near that region, particularly ILE230's CG2 and CYS231's N, but none of these are coming out close enough - I need to keep scanning nearby chain A atoms around that coordinate zone.

I check LYS241's CE and NZ against THR3's CG2, but the distances (4.33 and 4.55 Å) are still too far, and MET257 and LEU253 also don't seem to fit. It looks like THR3 only contacts MET257, possibly with LYS241 close by too.

Now I move to LYS4's region, mapping out its backbone and sidechain atoms (N, CA, C, O, CB, CG, CD, CE, NZ), and I find CYS231's SG contacts CD at 3.57 Å, while MET216's O contacts NZ, with ASP217 also nearby.

Continuing distance checks, I confirm ASN228, LEU229's N, and LEU229's CA all fall within contact range (2.85-3.97 Å) of LYS4's O, so they're already accounted for in my contact list.

Checking MET216's CB against NZ gives 3.32 Å, confirming M216 is already included, while ASP217's CA sits just outside the cutoff at 4.40 Å.

Now I'm scanning nearby glycine residues around positions 214-216 to see if any atoms fall within range of LYS4's CD/CE, but they all seem too far, confirming the LYS4 region is settled. Moving on, I'm pulling up the backbone coordinates for GLN5's N, CA, and C atoms to start checking that residue's contact region.

Continuing GLN5, I'm mapping out its side chain atoms (CB, CG, CD, OE1, NE2) and checking distances to nearby chain A residues like ASN228, GLY227, LEU229, and GLY226 — ASN228's backbone N and CB both fall within 4 Å of GLN5's OE1, so those count as contacts, while the others are too distant. That closes out GLN5 with just ASN228 as a neighbor, so I'm moving on to set up THR6's contact region next.

Now checking THR6's atoms against nearby chain A residues: GLU218's carbonyl oxygen, GLY227's oxygen, and LEU229's CD1 all land within range, and I'm confirming a couple of the borderline distances (GLU218 C to OG1, GLY227 C to OG1) to see which just barely make the 4 Å cutoff.

Checking ALA7's backbone atoms against nearby chain A residues: GLY226's CA and N both come within about 3.2-3.5 Å of ALA7's O, confirming another close contact already captured.

Now I'm mapping out ARG8's coordinates including its long side chain out to NE and CZ, to check its proximity to nearby chain A residues.

Looking at the guanidinium group of ARG8, I find several close contacts: GLU225's CG comes within range, GLY226's O to NE is 3.41Å, GLY227's CA to NH1 is 3.50Å, and LYS242's NZ to NH1 is 3.906Å. I'm now scanning other chain A atoms like CYS240's SG and LYS242's CD, but these turn out too far in the y-coordinate to be relevant contacts.

Now I'm shifting focus to the M3L9 residue's coordinates, checking its backbone and side chain atom positions to identify nearby contacts in that region.

Scanning chain A for residues within the target coordinate box, I've found Y203, S206, D207, D208, I209, Q219, A224, and E225 as candidates worth checking more closely.

ASP207's side chain carbons and oxygens end up too far from the ligand atom to count as contacts, while ASP208's backbone oxygen and ILE209's alpha and gamma carbons look like plausible contacts.

Continuing down the residue list, SER210 doesn't reach, but ALA224 and GLU225 both show close distances to the M3L nitrogen (around 2.8-3.9 Å), confirming contacts there. GLN219 also qualifies, while CYS220 and CYS223 fall short due to larger z-axis separations.

GLY226 misses the cutoff at 4.75 Å, and I'm re-checking TYR204's various atoms against CM2 more carefully - N, CA, CB, and C all come back too far (4.6-5.7 Å range), ruling out 204 entirely. Now I'm moving on to check MET205's side chain atoms against the nearby methyl carbons.

Shifting to the SER10 region, I'm laying out its coordinate bounds and cross-referencing against chain A residues with negative y-values, scanning through TYR203, ASP207, GLU218, GLU225, and LEU274 to find candidates whose y-coordinates dip below -14.

Only GLU218's OE2 qualifies, but its x and z values place it too far from SER10, so no contacts there. I move on to check ARG8's backbone oxygen against nearby chain A atoms, finding none close enough, then start scanning the y range -8 to -14 with x between -9 and 3 for residues like ASP207, ILE209, GLN219, and GLY226.

Working through this zone residue by residue, several fall within range: MET216's backbone oxygen, ASP217, GLU218, and parts of GLN219 all sit inside the region, along with ALA224's oxygen, GLU225's side chain atoms, and portions of GLY226, GLY227, ASN228, and LEU229.

Checking ASP212 more carefully: its atoms span roughly z -10 to -13, and measuring the distance from LYS4's NZ (chain C) to ASP212's OD2 gives about 3.57 Å — under the 4 Å cutoff, so this is a real contact between chain A's ASP212 and chain C.

I should double check the other nearby atoms too, but OD1 is too far. So D212 counts as a valid interface residue, and I need to go back and recheck other residues I may have dismissed too quickly in the same z-range.

Checking ARG211's coordinates against LYS4 NZ shows the x-distance is too large to be within range, so no contact there. I'm continuing to scan chain A residues 212 ASP and 213 SER coordinates for proximity to the chain C binding site.

CG distance also comes in around 4.54, still within range, so that spot checks out. Now I want to look at the region near ARG2's side chain more carefully, checking chain A residues in that x -14 to -16, y -8 to -11, z -6.5 to -8.6 pocket.

Residue 214 sits too far in z, so nothing qualifies there. Turning to ALA1's backbone atoms, I'm scanning chain A for anything in the x -14 to -20, y -1 to -6, z -4 to 2 box, and finding ILE256's O falls inside, along with ASP233's O nearby.

Continuing distance checks, I find ASP233's OD1 lands close at 3.79Å, while ALA1's CA, MET257's CA, and various ILE256 atoms (C, CG2) all fall just outside the 4.5-5Å contact threshold once I compute the actual dx/dy/dz vectors.

I check a few more nearby chain A residues like GLN262 and TRP263 but nothing qualifies, so region 1's contact set finalizes with ASP233, ILE256, and MET257.

I then verify residue 232's cysteine, some THR3-adjacent residues like ILE230/LYS241, and GLN5's CB/CG neighborhood against chain A candidates, but none of these are close enough to count as contacts either. Now I'm going back to double-check the ASP207 and TYR203 contacts.

Checking SER206's contact with M3L's methyl carbons confirms a hit, while MET205, residues 200-202, ILE209, and SER210 all come up too far from any chain C atoms. But GLN219's CD atom to M3L's CD comes out to about 3.63 Å, which confirms that contact, so I continue checking GLN219's OE1 as well.

OE1 to M3L CD lands at roughly 3.79 Å, also confirming a contact, while GLN219 CG to M3L CG checks out fine too. ASP208's backbone atoms mostly fall outside the 4 Å cutoff except the O atom at 3.906 Å, which just barely qualifies, so I'm moving on to look at ALA224 next.

For ALA224, only the O and CB atoms fall within range - CB checks out at 3.98 Å while CA and C are both too far. I'm now scanning CYS223 which shows no contacts, then shifting to look at whether ARG8's NH1 nitrogen has any nearby chain A atoms around the x -3 to -5, y -12 to -14, z 3-5 region, noting LYS242's NZ is already accounted for there.

Checking CYS243's SG and LYS242's CE both come up too far (4.14 Å), so those are clear. I'm then scanning ARG8's CB/CG region against GLU225 and GLY226 atoms, finding GLU225's CG and CD close (3.90-3.97 Å) but its OE2 and CB too distant, while GLY226's backbone nitrogen looks promising at roughly 3.37 Å.
